notes: Phase 1 look-dev frames and phase 2 textures. Candidates go to assets/src/generated/<id>/ (ignored); the approved one is copied to assets/src/selected/<id>.png and committed. Every look-dev frame must be checked against IRRI/PAU reference photos before approval; image models often draw wrong panicles, awns and tiller counts.

style.lookdev: Photorealistic documentary photograph, Punjab, India, late-morning sun with light haze, soft long shadows, natural colour, 35mm lens, sharp focus, no people, no text, no logos, no watermark.
style.cutaway: Educational museum-style cross-section: the image is split by a straight horizontal ground line at 65% of the image height; above it the field seen from eye level, below it a clean vertical cut through the soil like a soil monolith, showing roots in place.
style.texture: Seamless tileable texture, orthographic top-down view, perfectly even diffuse overcast light, no shadows from objects, no perspective, no vignette, no horizon, no text, fills the whole frame.
style.cutaway-texture: Flat orthographic straight-on photograph of a vertical cut face, even diffuse light, no vignette, no perspective, no text, fills the whole frame.
style.atlas: Botanical specimen flat-lay photographed straight down on a pure white seamless background, even shadowless studio light, nothing touching the frame edges, no text, no labels.

items.prompt: Freshly transplanted paddy rice field, variety like PR 126, late June. Hills of 3-4 rice seedlings about 20-25 cm tall, narrow light-green leaves, planted in neat rows 20 cm apart and 15 cm between hills, standing in 3-5 cm of muddy brown water that reflects a hazy sky. Earthen bund (daul) at the edge. Below ground: grey puddled hardpan layer about 15 cm down, short white fibrous roots just a few centimetres long.

Paddy rice at active tillering, mid July, each hill a dense upright clump of 12-20 tillers about 50-60 cm tall, deep green flat leaves, standing water between rows. Below ground: dense mat of fine white and pale-tan fibrous roots spreading 15-20 cm in saturated grey-brown mud, no taproot.

Rice at heading and flowering, late August, plants about 100 cm tall, flag leaves upright, slender panicles just emerged above the canopy with tiny cream-white anthers hanging from green spikelets. Shallow water or wet saturated soil between hills. Below ground: fibrous root mass reaching about 30 cm.

Mature rice ready for harvest, early October, panicles heavy and drooping in an arc, grains golden-straw coloured, upper leaves yellowing, lower leaves dry tan. Field drained, soil surface damp and cracked mud. Below ground: older brown fibrous roots in drying grey-brown soil.

Rice field just after combine harvest, mid October, rows of cut stubble about 25-30 cm high, loose pale-gold rice straw spread across the surface in uneven windrows, dry cracked soil. Below ground: dead brown root crowns.

Wheat seedlings emerging in mid November through a mulch of chopped rice straw, sown in straight rows 22.5 cm apart, each seedling a single narrow blue-green leaf about 8-10 cm tall. Dry light-brown alluvial loam. Below ground: seed with thin white seminal roots 10 cm long.

Wheat at tillering, late December, low dense tufts of blue-green leaves about 25-30 cm tall in straight rows, slight morning dew, rice straw mulch visible between rows. Below ground: crown roots and fine fibrous roots reaching 40-50 cm in light-brown loam.

Bread wheat at heading, late February, plants about 95-100 cm tall, glaucous blue-green stems and flag leaves, compact green spikes with straight awns 5-7 cm long, a few pale yellow anthers on spikelets. Below ground: fibrous roots reaching about 1 m, finer with depth.
Mature bread wheat in mid April, upright golden spikes with long straight golden awns, dry golden stems and leaves, dusty dry field, harsh bright sun. Below ground: dry pale soil, old brown roots.

Educational vertical cross-section through Punjab alluvial soil down to the water table, like a museum soil monolith: thin dark topsoil with roots, light-brown silty loam, a band with white calcium-carbonate nodules (kankar), damp darker zone, a thin capillary fringe, then saturated fine grey sand and gravel glistening with water. Clean straight cut faces, soft even light, no labels.

Farm tubewell at the edge of a Punjab paddy field: a blue-painted electric mono-block pump set on a small brick-and-cement plinth, steel starter box on a post, black electric cable to a concrete pole, a galvanised delivery pipe pouring clear water into a small rectangular brick outlet chamber that feeds an earthen field channel. Slight rust and water stains, mud splashes.

Wide flat Punjab farmland horizon, row of tall poplar and eucalyptus trees as a windbreak in the distance fading into warm atmospheric haze, pale blue-white sky with thin high cloud, late-morning sun.
Wet puddled paddy mud surface, smooth glossy grey-brown silt with shallow footprints-free ripples, a few tiny bits of rice straw, thin film of water.
Dry tilled light-brown alluvial loam soil surface with small crumbly clods, fine dust and small cracks.
Chopped rice straw mulch scattered thickly over brown soil, pale gold and tan straw pieces 5-15 cm long, random orientation.
Burnt rice field surface after straw burning, black char and grey-white ash over brown soil, a few charred stubble bases.
Short patchy grass and weeds growing on compacted brown earth of a field bund.

Straight-on view of a flat vertical cut face of layered alluvial soil, horizontal bands continuous across the whole width: dark brown topsoil at the very top, light-brown silty loam, a band with small white kankar nodules, damper darker brown, then grey wet sand at the bottom. Even shadowless light, no roots, no perspective, no sky, fills the whole frame.
Old Indian red clay brick wall in running bond with rough grey cement mortar, some cement smears and water stains.
Weathered grey cement plaster surface with fine cracks, damp stains and mud splashes.
Blue enamel-painted steel surface, chipped and scratched, with orange-brown rust patches and water streaks.
Close-up of woven white polypropylene fertilizer sack fabric, tight flat woven strips, slightly dusty.

Four rice leaf blades laid straight side by side vertically, long narrow flat leaves with a pale midrib and fine parallel veins, left to right: fresh deep green, light green, yellowing, dry straw-gold.
Four bread wheat leaf blades laid straight side by side vertically, flat leaves with parallel veins and slight waxy bloom, left to right: blue-green, green, yellowing, dry golden.

Three rice panicles laid flat, each a main axis with primary branches carrying oval spikelets, left to right: green at flowering with cream anthers, green-yellow filling grain, ripe golden-straw grain.
Three bread wheat spikes laid flat vertically with straight awns, left to right: green, yellow-green, ripe golden.
Washed fibrous root system of a cereal plant laid flat, many fine branching white and pale-tan roots with root hairs, spreading downward from a crown at the top.
